trust_decision.summary: Each get_path segment must be treated as one literal JSON object key or integer index, never as path syntax. At the pinned commit do_get_path builds the SQLite JSON path by joining raw segments with '.', so a segment containing '.', '[' or quotes changes which member json_extract reads.

landing_point.why: The summary names get_path and json_extract; this is the only place that concatenates a '$.' path string, inside do_get_path.

fix_sites.entry_point: Public Ash expression API: get_path(attr, [...]) / attr[:a][:b] in Ash.Query.filter, sort, calculations (e.g. calculate ... expr(get_path(stuff, [^arg(:key)]))) and Ash.load!, executed via the AshSqlite data layer; all three GetPath expr clauses (lib/sql_implementation.ex:103-151) funnel here
new private helper encode_json_path/encode_json_path_segment called only from do_get_path

O3_reason_to_dismiss: access_json_key (map equality compilation) already has a hand-written key guard for '$', quotes, backslashes and '' plus a test for those keys, so a solver will likely treat it as hardened, and as a separate comparison feature rather than get_path.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Integer segments must still index arrays ([n]), and ordinary and nested keys (stuff[:foo][:bar], atom segments) must keep resolving. In the O8 route, the fast '->' label path and the json_each fallback must both keep matching keys like '$.x', 'a"b' and ''. Rejecting dotted keys outright, or encoding integers as quoted keys, would break this legitimate behaviour.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Map equality, inequality and distinct-from filters against a literal map (stuff == ^%{...}) compile each key into SQLite '->' with the key bound as a text label. SQLite expands a label that does not start with '$' into the path '$.<label>' without quoting it, so a key containing '.' or '[n]' selects a nested member instead of the literal key. The guard only reroutes '$', '"', '\' and '' to json_each.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a different feature (structural map comparison, not get_path), it already has a deliberate key guard and a passing test (test/filter_test.exs:338-355), and the key is bound as a parameter, so it looks safe.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, about 270 lines above the fix site; reached through handle_map_comparison (lib/sql_implementation.ex:214-294, 398-450) and structural_match (lib/sql_implementation.ex:510-521)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A get_path-like accessor or sort helper that builds '$.' || key for '->>' extraction of scalar members
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The module already uses '->>' with literal paths, and a maintainer adding typed scalar extraction or JSON sorting would plausibly reuse the string-join idiom.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An atomic-update helper that renders json_set/json_remove(col, '$.' <> key, value) for partial map updates
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: list_expr and the map-literal clause show recent work on JSON writes in updates. A partial-update path is a natural next feature and would need the same path encoding.

O9_family: query injection: JSON path injection / key-to-path parser differential (CWE-943)

O10_build.toolchain: Elixir/Mix (mix.exs elixir ~> 1.11) with Hex deps ash_sql, ecto_sqlite3 (exqlite NIF, compiles bundled SQLite with a C compiler), optional ecto_libsql
O10_build.project_tests: ExUnit with an embedded SQLite file DB: test/calculation_test.exs:228-240 (get_path calcs) and test/filter_test.exs:338-355 (map comparison keys); resources in test/support/resources/post.ex

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Quote each string segment in do_get_path and stop, leaving access_json_key's '->' label route open (or reject keys containing '.', which breaks legitimate dotted keys).

out_of_scope_notes: The path is bound as a parameter (lib/sql_implementation.ex:854), so this is JSON-path selection, not raw SQL injection.
AshSql (an external dependency) holds the shared expression machinery. It was not inspected because it is another repository.
unverified: O8 depends on SQLite's '->' operator expanding a text label into '$.' plus the label without quoting it (my reading of SQLite json.c, abbreviated-path handling). The behaviour of the bundled exqlite SQLite version was not checked.
